chunks: Mansur al-Sayqal narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
“The pilgrim with us is of three types: a pilgrim performing tamattu‘, a pilgrim performing ifrad for hajj, and one driving the sacrificial animal; and the one driving it is the qarin.”

key_terms.الْقَارِنُ: one performing qiran, associated here with driving the sacrificial animal
key_terms.الْهَدْيِ: the sacrificial animal offered in hajj

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of hajj in Shi‘i hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith classifies hajj into three recognized forms in Shi‘i legal teaching: tamattu‘, ifrad, and qiran. It is significant because it defines the main categories of pilgrimage rites and identifies the sā'iq al-hady as the qarin.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2545 - Mansur al-Sayqal narrated from Abu Abdullah (as) that he said:

"The pilgrim falls into three categories with us: one performing tamattu‘ (combining ‘umrah and Hajj with a break in between), one performing ifrad (Hajj alone), and one driving the sacrificial animal (sā'iq al-hady), which is qirān (combining ‘umrah and Hajj without a break)."
